research_question: Does adding learned downstream sensitivity improve prospective prediction of Q.ANT CPU-backend numerical compatibility beyond accumulation term counts alone?
hypothesis: A model using stage-1 terms, stage-2 terms, and a sensitivity proxy measured from exact-reference activations plus trained head amplitudes will predict held-out end-to-end Q.ANT error better than a term-count-only baseline.
falsification_criterion: Not supported if the sensitivity-augmented model does not achieve lower held-out mean absolute prediction error than the term-count-only baseline.

proposed_method.protocol: Train held-out architectures first. Measure sensitivity proxy using exact-reference stage-1 perturbation proxy derived from trained weights/activations before any Q.ANT end-to-end evaluation. Freeze predictions from both baseline and augmented models, then evaluate Q.ANT outputs.
proposed_method.comparison: three-feature augmented model versus two-term baseline

limitations: Sensitivity proxy is not a full Jacobian norm.
CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
